cosy-lesson.title: Scientists Tracked Kids for 8 Years: The Screen Time Result

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Longitudinal ≠ Cross-sectional – conducted over a long period of time to track changes.

p.em: Example: Longitudinal studies help scientists understand developmental patterns over decades.

cosy-blockquote.p: Executive Functioning ≠ Impulsivity – cognitive processes including self-control, working memory, and focus.

p.em: Example: High executive functioning helps children solve complex puzzles.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sedentary ≠ Active – involving a lot of sitting and little physical exercise.

p.em: Example: A sedentary lifestyle can harm both physical health and attention span.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive Load ≠ Mental ease – the total amount of mental effort used in working memory.

p.em: Example: Fast-paced videos increase cognitive load in young minds.

cosy-blockquote.p: Regulation ≠ Dysregulation – the ability to manage and control emotional responses.

p.em: Example: Emotional regulation improves when children spend time outdoors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Exposure ≠ Protection – the state of experiencing or being subjected to an influence.

p.em: Example: Limiting screen exposure before bedtime leads to better sleep quality.

cosy-blockquote.p: Attentive ≠ Distracted – paying close attention to something.

p.em: Example: Children are more attentive when engaging in interactive storytelling.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intervention ≠ Neglect – action taken to improve a situation or prevent harm.

p.em: Example: Parental intervention can guide healthier digital media habits.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stimulation ≠ Boredom – encouraging activity, growth, or interest.

p.em: Example: Over-stimulation from rapid animations can cause fatigue.

cosy-blockquote.p: Correlation ≠ Independence – a mutual relationship or connection between two things.

p.em: Example: The study highlighted a strong correlation between outdoor play and focus.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the eight-year study, how does early screen exposure affect a child's executive functioning and attention?
★ How many hours of screen time did you have during your own childhood?

Why do scientists emphasize the difference between passive video viewing and interactive stimulation?
★ Do you feel that your current phone habits impact your daily attention span?

What role does parental intervention play in establishing healthy digital routines for young kids?
★ How do you set boundaries for yourself when using digital devices?

How can excessive sedentary behavior during early development influence long-term physical health?
★ What physical activities help you recharge after sitting at a desk all day?

Is there a clear correlation between early device usage and emotional regulation challenges later in school?
★ What strategies do you use when you feel overwhelmed by digital notifications?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Should schools implement mandatory digital detox periods to reduce students' daily cognitive load?
★ Would you support a total ban on smartphones in primary schools?

How might future longitudinal studies change our understanding of virtual reality in education?
★ How do you think technology in education will evolve over the next decade?

What measures can parents take to ensure children stay attentive during offline family activities?
★ What was your favorite non-digital hobby when growing up?

Could high screen exposure alter brain development patterns in ways that current research has not yet identified?
★ Are you concerned about how social media affects younger generations?

What public policy intervention would best balance technological literacy with healthy child growth?
★ If you were a regulator, what age limit would you set for personal smartphones?
